summary_paraphrase: At bedtime a small boy says good night to his family, the sky, the garden and every object in the house; huge shaggy monsters appear in his room, and instead of fleeing he tucks them in, befriends a little one and falls asleep on top of the biggest.

beats.function: good-night list widens to the world
he puts the monsters to bed

characters.name: Monu
characters.desire: to say good night to everything
characters.change: from frozen fear to tucking the monsters in

characters.name: the monsters
characters.relation_to_protagonist: bedtime fear made visible, then tucked in

characters.name: small monster
characters.relation_to_protagonist: the one under the bed, becomes a friend

humor_notes: Role reversal: the child puts the monsters to bed and kisses them; the bed perched on a sleeping monster.

repetition.description: 'Good night, Monu.' answers his good nights
repetition.why: the world answers him; the last return closes the book as the bedtime ritual

repetition.description: good-night list: say/wish/sleep tight to each thing in turn
repetition.why: a calming list that widens and then breaks off mid-line before the monsters

repetition.description: his bedtime words (sleep, sweet dreams) are given to the monsters and to himself
repetition.why: the ritual becomes the tool that tames the fear

notes: Four of thirteen pages are wordless (1, 8, 9, 11); the monsters exist only in the pictures.
A shadow in the kitchen (p5) foreshadows the monsters.
The last picture turns the threat into the bed itself.

strengths: a bedtime ritual list that calms by rhythm
the fear peak sits in the middle and the last pages wind down to sleep
the child tames the fear with the ritual he already owns; no adult intervenes
weaknesses: the monster sequence is carried by wordless pages; as text alone the middle is nearly empty
the mini-scare under the bed (p11) reopens tension close to the end

child_appeal_heuristic.rationale: Scores are the analyst's reading of the pages, not observations of children.
child_appeal_heuristic.label: Research heuristic — not validated

age_suitability.notes: Monsters are large and staring for three pages (research 4/5, about 2 on the engine's 0-3 scale) and are defused by the child's own action; the book itself is a bedtime book. As a text-only model the wordless middle would have to be told in words (m005).

metrics.lexicon_note: direct_address and sound_words are lexicon counts: a floor, not a measure. direct_address counts second-person words anywhere, dialogue included — it is not narrator-to-reader address

repetition.end_rhyme_note: heuristic: consecutive lines sharing a final two letters
